units.text: INT. TELEPHONE EXCHANGE - 1924 - NIGHT
Brass jacks, cord pairs, a wall of blinking lamps.
Gaslight on mahogany.
The air smells of hot wire.
CORDELIA ASHWORTH-BELL (20s, headset, high collar) stands at the board plugging cords with practiced speed.
Her supervisor, MRS. FENWICK (50s, iron-gray bun, pince-nez), watches from behind with a pocket watch.
Number, please.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: Connect me to the Admiralty. At once.
units.name: CAPTAIN WARRINGTON

units.text: One moment, sir.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: Cordelia, that line is reserved.
units.name: MRS. FENWICK

units.text: Mrs. Fenwick, he said at once.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: She plugs the cord.
A lamp flares red.
Miss, are you there? I hear nothing.
units.name: CAPTAIN WARRINGTON

units.text: Sir, the Admiralty is not answering.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: Then you disconnect, child.
units.name: MRS. FENWICK

units.text: But he'll hear the line go dead, Mrs. Fenwick.
units.name: CORDELIA

units.text: Miss, there is a fire at the harbor. Do you understand? Ring everyone.
units.name: CAPTAIN WARRINGTON

units.text: Cordelia looks at Mrs. Fenwick.
Mrs. Fenwick lowers the watch.
Ring everyone.
units.name: MRS. FENWICK

units.text: Cordelia seizes a bundle of cords and begins to plug, plug, plug, as the lamps all blaze at once.
